section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how college women's exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others influences their body image and eating behavior. The study found that exposure to non-body-focused others predicted more adaptive body image outcomes at both between-persons and within-persons levels, while day-to-day fluctuations in exposure to non-body-focused others (but not body-focused others) were associated with changes in eating and body image. The authors propose social learning theory as an explanation for why non-body-focused social interactions may be protective against maladaptive body image and eating behaviors.
